Definition: from G4859; to be harmonious, i.e. (figuratively) to accord (be suitable, concur) or stipulate (by compact):--agree (together, with).
BiblicalUsage: Jesus promises that if two of you agree on earth about anything they ask, it shall be done for them by His Father in heaven, and in the parable of the vineyard the householder reminds the labourer that he agreed with him for a penny. Agreement can be a holy thing, as when the prophets agree together in their witness, and it can be a wicked thing, as when Ananias and Sapphira agree together to tempt the Spirit of the Lord.
TheologicalSignificance: What grips me is that agreement in prayer is one of the great promises of the gospel, and I hold that I must be careful what I agree to, because agreement binds me to what I have joined. And I take the two agreements together as my warning and my promise: the prophets agree in witness, and Ananias and Sapphira agree in deception, and the difference is whom they agreed with.
